pages.title: This is Wärtsilä
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Our everyday lives depend on a steady supply of electricity and goods shipped to us from across the world. Yet, today the marine and energy sectors generate over a third of global greenhouse gases.
Over 80% of world trade is carried by sea. And global electricity demand is on track to double by 2050.
That’s why at Wärtsilä, we’ve chosen to dedicate ourselves to shaping the decarbonisation of marine and energy. We help our customers make a decarbonisation journey that is not just environmentally sustainable, but financially viable, too.
We already have most of the technology to decarbonise shipping and build a 100% renewable energy future. We develop engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels – such as ammonia, hydrogen and methanol. Our innovative technologies and services help our customers cut emissions, improve efficiency and reduce costs. Our engines on land ‘balance’ renewable energy by kicking in when the sun isn’t shining or wind isn’t blowing. This makes renewables more scalable and reliable.
But green is not black or white, and no single solution will carry us through the transition. Fossil fuels will play a role while sustainable alternatives become more available. As none of us alone have all the answers, we innovate along with our ecosystems and work to reduce global emissions while securing financial viability.
Explore the defining characteristics of our industries and what makes Wärtsilä well-positioned to support our customers in their decarbonisation journey.

Wärtsilä closes the transaction of the joint venture for its global Energy Storage business with RCT Solutions GmbH
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Technology group Wärtsilä has today closed the transaction of the joint venture for its Energy Storage business, following the agreement with German engineering company RCT Solutions GmbH announced on 15 June 2026. Under the arrangement, Wärtsilä and RCT Solutions each hold a 50% ownership stake in the joint venture, called Valo.
The joint venture combines Wärtsilä's global energy storage capabilities with RCT Solutions' engineering expertise and is designed to provide a strong platform for long-term growth in the rapidly evolving energy storage market.
Wärtsilä's Energy Storage business employs approximately 450 people globally, and in 2025, it generated net sales of EUR 694 million. The transaction represents less than 5% of Wärtsilä's total net assets.
Energy Storage ceased to be a separate reporting segment in Wärtsilä in the second quarter of 2026. Up to the completion of the transaction, the Energy Storage business is reported in discontinued operations. During the third quarter of 2026, Wärtsilä recognised a write-down of capitalised R&D related to the Energy Storage business before the establishment of the joint venture, rather than within the joint venture as previously expected. It is expected that the new joint venture will generate operating loss in 2026 and positive results towards the end of 2027.
With the transaction now completed, the joint venture will focus on executing its growth strategy and serving customers globally as an independent company jointly owned by Wärtsilä and RCT Solutions GmbH.
The joint venture transaction can be discussed in more details on Wärtsilä's pre-silent call today at 15:00 EEST; please register for the call here.

pages.title: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launch coordinated approach for faster U.S. data center power delivery
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Coordinated “Generator-to-Chip” approach integrates onsite generation, electrical infrastructure and engineering to help data center customers streamline development and save time compared to traditional delivery models.
Technology group Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants have developed an innovative “Generator-to-Chip” approach to help U.S. data center developers and operators bring scalable power capacity online faster. Designed around the AI load, the approach aligns onsite power generation, electrical infrastructure, automation, engineering and project execution from the outset. By connecting the power pathway from generation and electrical distribution to digital monitoring and the IT load, the approach reduces handoffs, improves coordination across critical interfaces and provides greater execution certainty. The combined approach can accelerate project schedules compared to traditional, sequential delivery models.
Driven by accelerating investment in AI, demand for new data center capacity is growing rapidly across the United States. At the same time, lengthy grid interconnection timelines and delays in critical power infrastructure are slowing projects and increasing the need for coordinated solutions that can deliver dependable power where and when it is needed.
Wärtsilä provides flexible, modular engine power plants that can deliver reliable onsite power generation, start rapidly and scale as data center demand grows. Schneider Electric contributes the integrated electrical architecture, automation and digital power management that coordinate power from generation to the AI load. Stanley Consultants provides technical and advisory services across the data center lifecycle, including engineering, permitting, design coordination, construction management, commissioning oversight and climate resilience expertise.
“For many data center projects, power has become the schedule. Developers need reliable solutions that can be planned, built and delivered at the pace that AI growth demands. This innovative, integrated approach marks a significant step forward: by bringing our complementary capabilities together from the outset, we can simplify execution, reduce handoffs and shorten timelines. Most importantly, it gives customers a faster, clearer path from project planning to operational capacity,” says Risto Paldanius, Vice President, Americas, Wärtsilä Energy.
“AI growth is increasing the scale and speed required of data center power infrastructure,” says Melton Chang, Executive Vice President, Power Systems at Schneider Electric. “An AI Energy Park starts with the load and coordinates generation, electrical infrastructure, automation and digital technologies as one system. This gives developers a scalable, grid-flexible path to bring high-density AI capacity online faster.”
“We are delighted to be part of a team that is focused on meeting our client’s business outcomes and community needs,” says Lance Sulzen, Vice President and Energy Market Leader at Stanley Consultants. “Integrated solutions help deliver functional, resilient, and scalable facilities effectively and efficiently. Taking a collaborative delivery approach helps us better identify risks, streamline interfaces and improve delivery confidence from concept to commissioning.”
Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants collectively bring expertise in power generation, electrical distribution, digital control and project execution that is relevant to modern data center development. Together, these capabilities demonstrate how data center operators can address requirements for speed, reliability, scalability and operational flexibility across grid-connected, islanded and hybrid configurations.

pages.title: Wärtsilä to deliver engines for Australia's largest-ever engine power plant to support the country's energy transition
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Technology group Wärtsilä has been selected to supply its flexible and highly efficient Wärtsilä 46TS engines for Australia’s largest-ever reciprocating engine power plant. The 300 MW plant will provide critical grid balancing and system security in Australia. The fast-starting flexible capacity provided by the Wärtsilä 46TS engines will enable greater integration of renewable energy into the power system. The order was booked by Wärtsilä in Q3 2026.
Australia is accelerating its energy transition, increasing the need for flexible capacity that can support renewable energy integration. Wärtsilä's gas engine generating sets are designed with future readiness in mind, including the ability to support grid stability as renewable energy capacity grows. By helping to maintain a stable and reliable power system, they can facilitate the integration of increasing shares of wind and solar power while supporting secure electricity supply.
When commissioned, the power plant will operate with 13 Wärtsilä 46TS-SG gas engines. This next-generation large-bore engine supports the security of supply and is designed to meet the evolving needs of the energy industry. It maintains strong performance in extreme ambient temperatures and at high-altitude locations and can currently operate with up to a 25 vol-% hydrogen fuel blend.
“Our engine technology combines the efficiency, flexibility and reliability needed to support Australia's evolving energy system,” says Frederic Carron, Vice President, Middle East and Asia at Wärtsilä Energy. “The Wärtsilä 46TS engine will help strengthen power system resilience, while its innovative modular design allows the plant to be easily expanded as the share of renewable energy increases.”
The Wärtsilä equipment is scheduled for delivery in early 2029, and the plant is expected to become fully operational the following year.

pages.title: This is Wärtsilä
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Our everyday lives depend on a steady supply of electricity and goods shipped to us from across the world. Yet, today the marine and energy sectors generate over a third of global greenhouse gases.
Over 80% of world trade is carried by sea. And global electricity demand is on track to double by 2050.
That’s why at Wärtsilä, we’ve chosen to dedicate ourselves to shaping the decarbonisation of marine and energy. We help our customers make a decarbonisation journey that is not just environmentally sustainable, but financially viable, too.
We already have most of the technology to decarbonise shipping and build a 100% renewable energy future. We develop engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels – such as ammonia, hydrogen and methanol. Our innovative technologies and services help our customers cut emissions, improve efficiency and reduce costs. Our engines on land ‘balance’ renewable energy by kicking in when the sun isn’t shining or wind isn’t blowing. This makes renewables more scalable and reliable.
But green is not black or white, and no single solution will carry us through the transition. Fossil fuels will play a role while sustainable alternatives become more available. As none of us alone have all the answers, we innovate along with our ecosystems and work to reduce global emissions while securing financial viability.
Explore the defining characteristics of our industries and what makes Wärtsilä well-positioned to support our customers in their decarbonisation journey.

Wärtsilä closes the transaction of the joint venture for its global Energy Storage business with RCT Solutions GmbH
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Technology group Wärtsilä has today closed the transaction of the joint venture for its Energy Storage business, following the agreement with German engineering company RCT Solutions GmbH announced on 15 June 2026. Under the arrangement, Wärtsilä and RCT Solutions each hold a 50% ownership stake in the joint venture, called Valo.
The joint venture combines Wärtsilä's global energy storage capabilities with RCT Solutions' engineering expertise and is designed to provide a strong platform for long-term growth in the rapidly evolving energy storage market.
Wärtsilä's Energy Storage business employs approximately 450 people globally, and in 2025, it generated net sales of EUR 694 million. The transaction represents less than 5% of Wärtsilä's total net assets.
Energy Storage ceased to be a separate reporting segment in Wärtsilä in the second quarter of 2026. Up to the completion of the transaction, the Energy Storage business is reported in discontinued operations. During the third quarter of 2026, Wärtsilä recognised a write-down of capitalised R&D related to the Energy Storage business before the establishment of the joint venture, rather than within the joint venture as previously expected. It is expected that the new joint venture will generate operating loss in 2026 and positive results towards the end of 2027.
With the transaction now completed, the joint venture will focus on executing its growth strategy and serving customers globally as an independent company jointly owned by Wärtsilä and RCT Solutions GmbH.
The joint venture transaction can be discussed in more details on Wärtsilä's pre-silent call today at 15:00 EEST; please register for the call here.

pages.title: Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants launch coordinated approach for faster U.S. data center power delivery
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Coordinated “Generator-to-Chip” approach integrates onsite generation, electrical infrastructure and engineering to help data center customers streamline development and save time compared to traditional delivery models.
Technology group Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants have developed an innovative “Generator-to-Chip” approach to help U.S. data center developers and operators bring scalable power capacity online faster. Designed around the AI load, the approach aligns onsite power generation, electrical infrastructure, automation, engineering and project execution from the outset. By connecting the power pathway from generation and electrical distribution to digital monitoring and the IT load, the approach reduces handoffs, improves coordination across critical interfaces and provides greater execution certainty. The combined approach can accelerate project schedules compared to traditional, sequential delivery models.
Driven by accelerating investment in AI, demand for new data center capacity is growing rapidly across the United States. At the same time, lengthy grid interconnection timelines and delays in critical power infrastructure are slowing projects and increasing the need for coordinated solutions that can deliver dependable power where and when it is needed.
Wärtsilä provides flexible, modular engine power plants that can deliver reliable onsite power generation, start rapidly and scale as data center demand grows. Schneider Electric contributes the integrated electrical architecture, automation and digital power management that coordinate power from generation to the AI load. Stanley Consultants provides technical and advisory services across the data center lifecycle, including engineering, permitting, design coordination, construction management, commissioning oversight and climate resilience expertise.
“For many data center projects, power has become the schedule. Developers need reliable solutions that can be planned, built and delivered at the pace that AI growth demands. This innovative, integrated approach marks a significant step forward: by bringing our complementary capabilities together from the outset, we can simplify execution, reduce handoffs and shorten timelines. Most importantly, it gives customers a faster, clearer path from project planning to operational capacity,” says Risto Paldanius, Vice President, Americas, Wärtsilä Energy.
“AI growth is increasing the scale and speed required of data center power infrastructure,” says Melton Chang, Executive Vice President, Power Systems at Schneider Electric. “An AI Energy Park starts with the load and coordinates generation, electrical infrastructure, automation and digital technologies as one system. This gives developers a scalable, grid-flexible path to bring high-density AI capacity online faster.”
“We are delighted to be part of a team that is focused on meeting our client’s business outcomes and community needs,” says Lance Sulzen, Vice President and Energy Market Leader at Stanley Consultants. “Integrated solutions help deliver functional, resilient, and scalable facilities effectively and efficiently. Taking a collaborative delivery approach helps us better identify risks, streamline interfaces and improve delivery confidence from concept to commissioning.”
Wärtsilä, Schneider Electric and Stanley Consultants collectively bring expertise in power generation, electrical distribution, digital control and project execution that is relevant to modern data center development. Together, these capabilities demonstrate how data center operators can address requirements for speed, reliability, scalability and operational flexibility across grid-connected, islanded and hybrid configurations.

pages.title: Wärtsilä to deliver engines for Australia's largest-ever engine power plant to support the country's energy transition
pages.main_text_excerpt:
Technology group Wärtsilä has been selected to supply its flexible and highly efficient Wärtsilä 46TS engines for Australia’s largest-ever reciprocating engine power plant. The 300 MW plant will provide critical grid balancing and system security in Australia. The fast-starting flexible capacity provided by the Wärtsilä 46TS engines will enable greater integration of renewable energy into the power system. The order was booked by Wärtsilä in Q3 2026.
Australia is accelerating its energy transition, increasing the need for flexible capacity that can support renewable energy integration. Wärtsilä's gas engine generating sets are designed with future readiness in mind, including the ability to support grid stability as renewable energy capacity grows. By helping to maintain a stable and reliable power system, they can facilitate the integration of increasing shares of wind and solar power while supporting secure electricity supply.
When commissioned, the power plant will operate with 13 Wärtsilä 46TS-SG gas engines. This next-generation large-bore engine supports the security of supply and is designed to meet the evolving needs of the energy industry. It maintains strong performance in extreme ambient temperatures and at high-altitude locations and can currently operate with up to a 25 vol-% hydrogen fuel blend.
“Our engine technology combines the efficiency, flexibility and reliability needed to support Australia's evolving energy system,” says Frederic Carron, Vice President, Middle East and Asia at Wärtsilä Energy. “The Wärtsilä 46TS engine will help strengthen power system resilience, while its innovative modular design allows the plant to be easily expanded as the share of renewable energy increases.”
The Wärtsilä equipment is scheduled for delivery in early 2029, and the plant is expected to become fully operational the following year.
